title: The shapers: raw entries into records, each shaped once and streamed, never holding a secret, a contact or a table's rows
request: Every raw entry into normalised records with provenance, capture flags and split, scrubbed, rebuildable byte for byte.
plan: One record per JSON line, per JSON file version, per test-run line.
Redact words, remove cell-quoting keys and printed tables, keep ids, hashes and times.
Seal labels with their decisions, drafts with their projects.
Shape each entry once; rebuild whole when the shapers' version changes.

decisions.decision: Each raw entry is shaped once and streamed into chunks under 20 MB.
decisions.why: Raw entries never change; a 280 MB transcript re-shaped every hour would take minutes and gigabytes, and a 280 MB file cannot be pushed.

decisions.decision: Decisions and teachers are rebuilt whole every run.
decisions.why: A record's split depends on others: a label on its decision, a draft on the project it became.

decisions.decision: A rebuild is written beside the old records and swapped in.
decisions.why: No stale file survives a change of the shapers.

change: dclab_rnd.store.shapers (Context, _body with database rows and transcript fields, _tables_out, streamed _opened with its hash, _Writer chunks, per-line errors, the records lock, version marks).

findings.defect: A key inside a gzip source reached the records.
findings.scenario: A test run's own gzip with a key in a unit's output.
findings.cause: Credentials were removed from the compressed bytes.
findings.fix: Each line is opened, then cleaned.

findings.defect: Contacts and table rows from tool outputs reached the records.
findings.scenario: A git log's e-mail and a CSV printed by head in a transcript's stdout.
findings.cause: Only a few text keys were redacted.
findings.fix: Every string of a transcript redacted, printed tables replaced by their size, unparsed lines by their hash.

findings.cause: request was a text key and ids were not exempt.
findings.fix: Ids, hashes and times are never redacted.

findings.defect: PostgreSQL's decisions got no group or split, and labels the wrong type.
findings.scenario: db/decision_label rows typed as decisions, group None.
findings.cause: Database rows keep their document under doc and their ids as project_id.
findings.fix: Rows lifted and renamed; typed by table; every decision's group gathered before any label.

findings.defect: A draft and the project it became could sit in different splits.
findings.scenario: A decision on draft d1 grouped draft:d1, the same table's later decisions project:p1.
findings.cause: The draft-to-project map was not given.
findings.fix: The map from every draft's newest version and the decisions holding both.

findings.defect: One bad line half-shaped an entry.
findings.scenario: A project given as an object stopped the entry midway.
findings.fix: Per line, its reason kept; ids coerced to text.

findings.scenario: A file of an old month survived a forced rebuild.

findings.defect: Transcript records had no split and the wrong time.
findings.scenario: Every line split None, its time the capture's.
findings.cause: The session and its time were under other names.
findings.fix: sessionId and timestamp read as session and at.

findings.defect: The hourly run could not handle 1.1 GB.
findings.scenario: Minutes of CPU, gigabytes of memory, a 280 MB month file.
findings.cause: Everything was re-shaped and held in memory.

findings.scenario: A deleted intern session's records looked live.
findings.cause: Only projects and drafts were compared.

findings.defect: Times were redacted as phone numbers.
findings.cause: Every string of a transcript was redacted.
findings.fix: Times are left as they are, like ids.

outcome: Every raw entry becomes clean, linked, sealed records once, streamed, rebuildable from raw alone.
lessons: Splits that depend on other records need a first pass before any record is written.
risks: A printed table without separators is not recognised as a table.
